title: Digital nomad visas: which countries are easiest to move to now?
summary: Find out which countries are the easiest to move to with a digital nomad visa.
body_markdown:
Not long ago, if you told someone you were working from a beach, they’d assume you were on a sabbatical or freelancing under the radar. Today? You might just be on a[digital nomad](https://grey.co/blog/beyond-the-basics-smart-ways-to-grow-as-a-digital-nomad) visa.


Since the rise of remote work, dozens of countries have rolled out special visa schemes targeting location-independent professionals, inviting them to live and work legally. If you're itching to pack your bags and plug in from somewhere new, here’s a breakdown of the easiest countries to move to right now, plus what makes them remote worker-friendly.


**Also read:**[Beyond the basics: Smart ways to grow as a digital nomad](https://grey.co/blog/beyond-the-basics-smart-ways-to-grow-as-a-digital-nomad)


## What is a digital nomad visa?


A digital nomad visa is a residence permit that allows remote workers, typically freelancers, business owners, or full-time employees with foreign clients or employers, to live in another country while working online.


Unlike tourist visas ([which often prohibit remote work](https://grey.co/blog/can-you-work-remotely-while-travelling-on-a-tourist-visa) ),digital nomad visas are tailor-made for location-independent professionals and usually allow stays of 6–24 months, with the option to extend.


**Also read:**[How to travel the world without quitting your job](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-apply-for-a-digital-nomad-visa-in-portugal)


## What makes a country easy for digital nomads?


“Easy” means different things to different people, but when we talk about easy digital nomad visas, we’re looking at:


- **Simple application process:** Online submissions, minimal paperwork, quick approvals.
- **Low-income requirements:** Many nomad visas require proof of steady income, some more than others.
- **Reasonable fees** : No one wants to pay huge amounts just to work abroad.
- **Access to essentials:** Strong internet, remote-friendly infrastructure, coworking spaces, and an international community.


## Top countries with the easiest digital nomad visas in 2025


### 1. Portugal


[Portugal’s D7 visa](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-apply-for-a-digital-nomad-visa-in-portugal) is one of Europe’s most flexible long-term visa options. The country also offers excellent healthcare, interesting cities, and a growing remote work culture.


- Minimum income required: About €820/month
- Visa duration: 1 year, renewable for up to 5 years
- Perks: Path to residency, visa-free Schengen travel
- Application tip: Although the D7 wasn’t designed just for digital nomads, many use it for that purpose.


### 2. Spain


Spain launched its o[fficial digital nomad visa](https://grey.co/blog/how-to-apply-for-a-digital-nomad-visa-in-spain) in 2023, with one of the lowest income thresholds in Western Europe and access to a special tax scheme.


- Minimum income required: About €2,200/month
- Visa duration: Up to 1 year, extendable to 5 years
- Perks: 15% tax rate for 4 years, access to public services
- Application tip: Your employer or clients must be located outside Spain.


### 3. Costa Rica


The[Rentista visa](https://residencies.io/residency/costa-rica/temporary-residency/cr1) used to be the go-to, but[Costa Rica’s new digital nomad visa](https://www.visitcostarica.com/digital-nomads) is tailor-made for remote workers. The country is peaceful and naturally stunning and is already a hotspot for US-based nomads.


- Minimum income required: $3,000/month (or $4,000 for families)
- Visa duration: 1 year, renewable
- Perks: No local tax on foreign income, easy renewal process
- Application tip: Proof of income must come from outside Costa Rica.


### 4. Mauritius


Mauritius offers a free premium[visa for remote workers](https://grey.co/blog/mauritius-digital-nomad-visa) who want to live in paradise for up to a year. Some of the requirements include:


- Minimum income required: $1,500/month
- Visa duration: 12 months
- Perks: No visa fee, stunning island life, strong expat support
- Application tip: Must show a return ticket and accommodation booking.


### 5. Estonia


Estonia was the first EU country to launch an official digital nomad visa.


- Minimum income required: €4,500/month (last 6 months)
- Visa duration: 1 year
- Perks: Strong digital government, vibrant startup scene
- Application tip: It’s one of the most transparent application processes in Europe.


## Tips before you apply


- **Check health insurance requirements:** Many visas require private insurance before arrival.
- **Get your income proof ready:** This is often bank statements, invoices, or employment letters.
- **Know your tax obligations:** Some countries don’t tax foreign income, others do.
- **Look for community:** Coworking spaces, Slack groups, and expat meetups can make all the difference.
